title: Add gap-to-planning-stage tracing and effect check to athena-core
summary: Reading: the owner wants logged gaps (interventions, introspections, rejections, ratings) traced to the planning stage that missed them, and a check of whether refinements reduced later gaps. This run does only the pure core: a new athena-core module that traces each gap to one of five stages and reports a refinement effect. The role, CLI, queueing and docs are follow-ups.

defaults_applied.how: Unit tests in the module; cargo test, clippy and fmt --check must pass.
One module only; role, CLI and docs deferred.
Criteria run tests that assert the traced stage and the effect verdict.
An empty sample never reports reduced.
Plain std Rust, no new crate needed.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I listed crates/athena-core/src (steward.rs, audience.rs, introspect.rs, plan.rs, reading.rs, proposals.rs, lib.rs) and crates/athena-data/src (roles.rs, records.rs). Existing roles (steward, audience) are in athena-core with role definitions in athena-data/roles.rs. I did not read their bodies, so the producer must read steward.rs and introspect.rs and match their gap and record types. Entry point: a pure function over gap values; no resolution or probing order is involved. The module adds no record or data file under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not triggered. The stage and reduction results are computed directly from the gap values, not through a stand-in.
Goal and audience: the owner judges whether the next plan avoids repeat misses. This job delivers the tracing and effect-check logic they can test.
Scope is cut to one deliverable because a median above verifier_timeout_s (2400s) is refused. Role definition, CLI command, refinement queueing, and docs are follow-up requests.
Stage mapping is rule-based on gap kind and keywords in the gap text, with a deterministic default stage when nothing matches, for example outcome check.
This adds no refusal rule and edits no governance file or prompt file.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test -p athena-core gap_audit: a test gives one gap of each source kind (intervention, introspection, rejection, rating) and asserts each traces to exactly one of the five stages: reading, decomposition, assumptions, criteria, outcome check.

Run cargo test -p athena-core gap_audit: tests assert distinct gap texts trace to distinct stages, for example a missed-requirement text to reading and a wrong-check text to outcome check, and an unmatched gap gets the documented default stage.

Run cargo test -p athena-core gap_audit: the effect check returns Reduced when same-kind gaps fall after a refinement, NotReduced when they stay equal or rise, and NoEvidence for an empty before or after sample. An empty sample never returns Reduced.
Run cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check: all pass with no warnings.
Grep crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs for the gap_audit module declaration. The module's doc comment names the five stages and four gap sources for an outside reader.

out_of_scope: A new role definition in athena-data roles and its cadence and ladder limit
A CLI command and fake-agent end-to-end test
Queueing refinement work items or proposals from traced gaps
Editing prompt files or defaults.toml to refine the stages
A docs/design page on the role and its alternatives
departures: Smaller scope than the reference, with one module and tests, so a slightly lower cost and a shorter time.
